title: Effect of fire factors (smoke, ash, charcoal and heat) on seeds of plant species
author: Cruz, Riveiro, et al.

steps.title: Collect and store seeds
steps.instruction: Collect seeds of the target plant species in the field during their fruiting period, release them from the fruit, and keep them until treatments are applied. Store seeds in paper bags either at ~25 °C (room temperature) or at 4 °C (refrigerator) depending on the species: Leguminosae, Cistaceae and other hard‑seeded species can be kept at room temperature; Fagaceae, Betulaceae and Pinaceae require cold storage for long‑term preservation; Salicaceae seeds lose viability after ~15 days at room temperature and should be frozen. Visually inspect seeds and discard any that are damaged or not fully mature.

steps.title: Prepare fire‑factor treatments
steps.instruction: Set up seed treatment groups according to the combinations listed in Table 1, applying the specified heat, smoke, ash, and charcoal conditions.

substeps.instruction: Heat 80 °C for 5 min; expose seeds to smoke for 5 min (smoke obtained from the studied species); add ash amount 1; no charcoal.
Heat 80 °C for 10 min; expose seeds to smoke for 10 min (smoke obtained from the studied species); add ash amount 2; no charcoal.
Heat 110 °C for 5 min; expose seeds to smoke for 15 min (smoke obtained from Ulex europaeus); add ash amount 3; no charcoal.
Heat 110 °C for 10 min; no smoke exposure; add ash amount 4; no charcoal.
Heat 150 °C for 5 min; no smoke exposure; add ash amount 5; no charcoal.
Heat 150 °C for 10 min; no smoke, ash, or charcoal.
Heat 200 °C for 5 min; no smoke, ash, or charcoal.
Heat 200 °C for 10 min; no smoke, ash, or charcoal.
